info.title: Slotlock
info.description: Calendars agents cannot double-book. The "Agent tools" operations are the Slotlock MCP tools; the "Application" operations (resources, bookable hours, holds, reservations, coverage and maintenance) need an API key with the admin scope. An error is RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) whose `code` names it, also as `{"error":{"code":…}}`; an overlap names the `resource_id`, `start` and `end` it refused. A write that waits for a person answers 428 `confirmation_required`.

baseUrl.description: The server's public URL (SLOTLOCK_PUBLIC_URL), without a trailing slash.

tags.name: Agent tools
tags.description: What an agent does: the MCP tools and A2A skills.

tags.name: Application
tags.description: What the application around the agents does. Needs the admin scope; never offered to agents.

get.description: List resources visible to the authenticated tenant principal, with the pool each belongs to (a vehicle class, a room type). With pool, only that pool's members, in the order slotlock_book_pool tries them.

post.description: Create the resource with this external reference, or update its time zone if the tenant already has it. Repeating the call changes nothing more. visibility is shared (the default: agents list and book it) or private (agents never see it), fixed at creation: naming another for an existing resource answers 409 resource_visibility_conflict.

get.description: Return privacy-minimized busy intervals and explicit coverage certainty.
Find the earliest certain interval that satisfies the requested duration (up to the 367-day search window, so a multi-month rental slot can be found).

List up to `limit` certain slots of the requested duration, earliest first across the resources, each one free of busy time and inside the resource's hours, to offer a person a choice. With require_free, only times when at least that many of the resources are free together, each slot naming them in resource_ids: every resource for a booking that needs them all (book it with slotlock_book_together), or any n of them. No slot is listed unless every resource's coverage is certain.

post.description: Hold up to five candidate slots for a short time (30-900 seconds) while a person chooses, as alternatives in one group: each free one is held, the others are listed with why not. Book one by passing its hold_id to slotlock_create_event, which releases the rest; unbooked holds expire on their own. A hold is yours alone, and you may have 20 live at once.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stands in for idempotency_key: a Structured Field String (`"8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324"`, draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-08) or the bare key; when both are sent they must be equal. A retry with the same key and request answers what the first did; the same key with another request is 422 idempotency_conflict. An event write keeps its key for 30 days (maintenance removes it after that), a hold until the hold would have expired, is released or is confirmed. Where the key is required and neither is sent: 400 idempotency_key_required.

post.description: Book the same time on 2-20 resources at once, all or none: a van with its driver, a room with its projector. If any of them is taken, nothing is booked, and the refusal names that resource_id. Find such a time with slotlock_find_available_slots and require_free. A retry with the same idempotency_key answers the same events.

post.description: Book any one member of a pool (a vehicle class, a room type) for a time: members are tried in a fixed order and the first that is free and allows the booking is booked, in one transaction, so a class sells out exactly at its number of members. The event names the member booked. 409 pool_full when none is free; 404 pool_not_found when the pool has no member you may book. A retry with the same idempotency_key answers the same event.

get.description: How many members of a pool (a vehicle class, a room type) are free across a window: the window split where that number changes, each part with how many are free, and coverage certainty. Book one with slotlock_book_pool. 404 pool_not_found when the pool has no member you may book.

delete.description: Release one of your holds, and the rest of its group, at once instead of letting them expire. `released` is false when it was already gone.

get.description: List bounded events intersecting a time window.

post.description: Create an event of up to 3,660 days (a booking, lease or long rental); opaque occurrences use the database overlap arbiter.

get.description: Read one tenant-scoped event by stable identifier.

patch.description: Apply an expected-revision event patch and rematerialize occupancy atomically. With expected_resource_id, the resource you read the event on, an event since moved elsewhere is not found.

delete.description: Tombstone an event at an expected revision so stale sync cannot resurrect it.

get.description: One resource of the tenant, archived or not, with its own weekly bookable hours and its visibility.

delete.description: Delete a resource with its history (past bookings, coverage, cancelled events), freeing its place under the tenant's resource limit. Refused with 409 resource_in_use while a booking on it has not ended, a hold on it is live, or a calendar event is on it: cancel or move those first. deleted is false when the tenant has no such resource, deleted already, say.

post.description: Take a resource out of use: no list shows it and it takes no new booking, hold or event (409 resource_archived), while what is on it stays and can still be cancelled or released. Archiving it again keeps the first time.
Put an archived resource back in use. Restoring one in use changes nothing.

get.description: The time a resource of the tenant, private ones included, is occupied in a window of at most 367 days, by start: bookings with their turnaround, live holds, and calendar events. Adjacent intervals are not merged. More than 10,000 answers 400 calendar_work_limit: narrow the window. Free/busy with coverage, for the resources agents see, is slotlock_get_free_busy.

put.description: Give one resource its own weekly bookable hours. `null` makes it use the server's default; `[]` makes it never bookable. Each rule is weekly with BYDAY, in the resource's time zone: start_minutes after midnight, lasting duration_minutes.

get.summary: Export a resource's bookable hours as iCalendar
get.description: One resource's own weekly bookable hours as an iCalendar VAVAILABILITY (RFC 7953) for a calendar or scheduling tool: an AVAILABLE per rule, its DTSTART's TZID the resource's IANA time zone. `null` when the resource uses the server's default.

put.summary: Import a resource's bookable hours from iCalendar
put.description: Set one resource's own weekly bookable hours from an iCalendar VAVAILABILITY (RFC 7953), as slotlock_set_resource_availability does from rules: each AVAILABLE a weekly RRULE with a start time and DTEND or DURATION. Times must be in the resource's time zone (its TZID) or floating. 400 invalid_availability names what weekly hours cannot say: a bounded VAVAILABILITY, RDATE, EXDATE, a single window, another zone.

Set what a booking on one resource must satisfy from now on: minimum notice, how far ahead, the step starts fall on (from local midnight in the resource's time zone), the turnaround kept free after each booking, and whether bookings must lie inside its hours. `null` clears them. Holds, reservations, moves and agents' events are refused with the rule they break; searches offer only what they allow.

Make a resource a member of a pool, a class of interchangeable resources such as a vehicle class or a room type, or take it out (`null`). Agents book the class with slotlock_book_pool, which takes the first member free; the class's capacity is its number of members. A resource is in one pool at most; pool names are 1-100 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'.

get.description: The tenant's pools by name, each with its capacity: how many members it has that are not archived.

What happened on one of the tenant's resources, newest first: each hold, booking and event made, moved, confirmed, released or cancelled, when, by whom (the API key or agent), and for a change what it was before. Kept 30 days. Pass next_before as before for older entries.
What happened to one booking, by its reference, newest first: made, moved, cancelled, when and by whom, as slotlock_get_resource_history.
What happened to one calendar event of the tenant, by its id, newest first: created, changed, cancelled, when and by whom, as slotlock_get_resource_history.

put.description: Set the weekly bookable hours of every resource the tenant has, as slotlock_set_resource_availability does for one. `null` makes them all use the server's default. Returns how many resources changed.

post.description: Occupy a window without booking it, for example while a customer pays. The hold blocks every other booking until it expires (the database clock, ttl_seconds from now), is confirmed, or is released. buffer_after_minutes keeps the time after it busy as well, and a confirmed hold keeps it. A taken window answers 409 overlap. With an idempotency key (the Idempotency-Key header or idempotency_key), a retry answers the hold the first request made, until that hold would have expired, is released or is confirmed; the same key with another request is 422 idempotency_conflict.

idempotency_key.description: A retry identity, also accepted as the Idempotency-Key header: the same key with the same request answers what the first did; with another request, 422 idempotency_conflict.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stands in for idempotency_key: a Structured Field String (`"8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324"`, draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-08) or the bare key; when both are sent they must be equal. A retry with the same key and request answers what the first did; the same key with another request is 422 idempotency_conflict. An event write keeps its key for 30 days (maintenance removes it after that), a hold until the hold would have expired, is released or is confirmed. Where the key is required and neither is sent: 400 idempotency_key_required.

get.description: One of the tenant's live holds. An expired, confirmed, released or unknown one answers 404 hold_not_found; a confirmed one is a reservation whose reference is the hold's id.

delete.description: Free a held window. released is false when the hold was already gone: expired, confirmed or released.

get.description: The live holds on one of the tenant's resources, by start then id, a page at a time: pass next_cursor as cursor for the next page, until it is null.

post.description: Turn an unexpired hold into a confirmed reservation, whose reference is the hold's id at revision 1: move or cancel it with the reservation routes by that reference (DELETE /v1/reservations/{hold_id}?revision=2 cancels it). Confirming it again answers the same reservation, so a retry is safe. An expired hold answers 409 hold_expired; a released or unknown one, 404 hold_not_found.

get.description: The tenant's booking with this reference as it now is, at its current revision: move it at that revision plus 1. A cancelled or unknown reference, or a calendar event's time, answers 404 reservation_not_found.

put.description: Book the reservation with this reference (revision 1), or move it (the next revision: the current one plus 1). Sending the same reservation at its current revision again changes nothing (replayed: true). A taken window answers 409 overlap and leaves a moved reservation where it was. buffer_after_minutes keeps the time after it busy as well.

delete.description: Cancel the reservation with this reference at the next revision (the current one plus 1). Cancelling leaves a tombstone, so a delayed booking cannot bring it back; repeating the cancel answers cancelled: false. Use a new reference for a new reservation.

get.description: The tenant's bookings on one resource whose time, turnaround included, meets a window of at most 367 days, by start then id, a page at a time: pass next_cursor as cursor for the next page, until it is null. Calendar events are not bookings; slotlock_list_tenant_events lists them.

post.description: Claim a booking by its reference: the customer has arrived or picked up. On a resource whose booking rules set check_in_minutes, a booking not checked in that long after its start is released by maintenance (reservation.no_show on the feed) and offered to the waitlist. Check-in opens an hour before the start (409 check_in_not_open before then) and moving the booking to another start clears it. Checking in again keeps the first time; a booking that has ended answers 409 reservation_ended.

Wait for a window on one resource (resource_id) or on any member of a pool (pool) that is taken now. When it comes free (a booking cancelled, a hold released or expired, a no-show), the entries waiting for it are offered in the order they joined: the first gets a hold of it for holder_ref, for offer_ttl_seconds (default 900), and the feed says so (waitlist.offered, with hold_id): confirm the hold to book it. An entry whose window starts first expires (waitlist.expired). A holder may wait for 20 windows at once (409 waitlist_limit_reached); a window is at most 31 days.

get.description: The tenant's waitlist entries in the order they are offered (oldest first), with what each was offered: optionally only those of one resource, pool or holder.

delete.description: Stop waiting. A hold offered and not yet confirmed is released with the entry, and the time offered to the next who waits; one confirmed is a booking and stays. left is false when there was no such entry.

put.description: Record that the events of an external calendar (source) are complete for a window of a resource, at that source's revision. Free/busy calls time unproven, not free, until every source a resource requires covers it. Revisions only go forward; repeating one changes nothing.

get.summary: A resource's coverage and its health
get.description: Each external calendar (source) that records coverage of a resource: the window it covers, when it was last read, its last error, and whether it is stale (not read for a day, so the time it covers is unproven, not free). A source that goes stale is also put on the change feed once, as coverage.stale, until it is read again.

post.summary: Record a failed read of a source
post.description: Record that reading an external calendar failed (it answered 500, a token expired): kept as the source's last error, shown by slotlock_get_coverage, while its coverage stays as it was. 404 coverage_not_found for a source that has never recorded coverage of the resource.

get.summary: List a resource's events, every key's
get.description: The calendar events on one of the tenant's resources with an occurrence in a window of at most 367 days, whichever key wrote them (a revoked one's included), by start then id, a page at a time: pass next_cursor as cursor for the next page, until it is null.

get.summary: Get any event of the tenant
get.description: One of the tenant's events by its id (the id slotlock_list_tenant_events gives), whichever key wrote it. A cancelled or unknown one answers 404 event_not_found.

delete.summary: Cancel any event of the tenant
delete.description: Cancel one of the tenant's events by its id, whichever key wrote it (a revoked key's included, without charging its quota), at the revision you last read (expected_revision). Its owner cannot create it again. With expected_resource_id, an event since moved to another resource answers 404 event_not_found. Needs an idempotency key (the Idempotency-Key header or idempotency_key): a retry with it answers the first cancellation (replayed: true).

schema.description: A retry identity, also accepted as the Idempotency-Key header: the same key with the same request answers what the first did; with another request, 422 idempotency_conflict.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stands in for idempotency_key: a Structured Field String (`"8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324"`, draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-08) or the bare key; when both are sent they must be equal. A retry with the same key and request answers what the first did; the same key with another request is 422 idempotency_conflict. An event write keeps its key for 30 days (maintenance removes it after that), a hold until the hold would have expired, is released or is confirmed. Where the key is required and neither is sent: 400 idempotency_key_required.

get.description: One of the tenant's events as a JSCalendar Event (RFC 8984), the JSON form of a calendar event: uid is its id, sequence its revision, start a local time in timeZone with an exact duration, its people participants, its reminders alerts, its recurrence recurrenceRules and recurrenceOverrides (and the RRULE verbatim as slotlock.pylota.io:rrule). A cancelled or unknown one answers 404 event_not_found.

The key's tenant: its reference, and whether it is suspended. A suspended tenant may read and writes nothing (403 tenant_suspended); only the server's operator suspends a tenant or lifts a suspension (slotlock tenant suspend).

post.description: Delete everything the key's tenant has, at once and for good: resources, holds, bookings, events, coverage and every API key, this one included. confirm_tenant_ref must be the tenant's reference (slotlock_get_tenant), or it answers 400 invalid_confirmation. Off unless the server allows it (403 tenant_erasure_disabled; slotlock serve does not: its operator runs slotlock tenant erase). A suspended tenant cannot erase itself (403 tenant_suspended). Erasing again deletes nothing.

Extend recurring events to the rolling horizon and prune what the retention window no longer needs, for the caller's tenant. Run it at least daily (slotlock serve does). capped is true when there was more than one call does: call again.

get.description: What changed in the tenant, oldest first, as CloudEvents: holds made, confirmed, released or expired; bookings made, moved or cancelled; calendar events created, changed or cancelled (ids, times and states, never titles or attendees). Pass next_cursor as cursor to read on; it is returned even when nothing is new, so poll with it. Only changes of transactions that have ended are listed, so following the cursor never skips one. Changes are kept 30 days: an older cursor answers 410 cursor_expired, so start again without one.

post.description: Send the changes slotlock_list_changes lists from now on to an https URL, each as a CloudEvent signed as Standard Webhooks (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature), in order, until a 2xx. A failure is retried with backoff; after 24 hours of failures, or a 410, the webhook is disabled and the feed records webhook.disabled. The secret is returned here only. At most 10 per tenant.

get.description: The tenant's webhooks with how delivery is going: failed attempts, the last status, and whether and why one is disabled.

delete.description: Stop sending to a webhook. deleted is false when the tenant has no such webhook.

post.description: Send to a disabled webhook again, from the first change it did not accept. 404 webhook_not_found when the tenant has no such webhook; 409 changes_pruned when what it missed is older than the 30 days the feed keeps, since it would skip those unseen: delete it, add it again, and read what it missed from slotlock_list_changes.

bearer.description: A Slotlock API key (`slk_…`) or the server token. `x-slotlock-scope` on each operation names the scope it needs.

type.description: The problem type: a tag URI, one per code.

code.description: Why the operation did not run.

resource_id.description: An overlap: the resource it refused.

start.description: An overlap: the start it refused.

end.description: An overlap: the end it refused.

Error.description: The operation did not run; `code` says why.

Link.description: Where the error codes are documented (`rel="describedby"`).
